label: Impulse!
rationale: The one leader date Roy Haynes himself named as his favourite, and the record that puts a drummer who shaped the music's pulse — from Bird and Pres to Monk and Coltrane — in front of his own band, with Roland Kirk as the frontline. Cross-tradition consensus holds at 4.5/5 from AllMusic, 4.5/5 from Down Beat (Oct 25, 1962), 3.5/5 from the Penguin Guide and 4/5 from the Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide (all ratings via S1), and AllMusic's reviewer calls it 'a splendid sounding 1962 set' in which Haynes' drumming 'is absolutely wonderful here, lightly dancing around the other instruments' (S2). Lineage is direct and audible in this canon: the quartet grew out of jam sessions at the Five Spot and Haynes took the idea to producer Bob Thiele himself (S4), placing it a month after Coltrane's 'Coltrane' sessions and the same season as Kirk's own Impulse! debut; the middle brace of modal pieces (Raoul, Snap Crackle, Long Wharf) reach forward to the post-bop canon that follows. Session gravity: Kirk on tenor, manzello, stritch and flutes, Tommy Flanagan (Coltrane's pianist on Giant Steps and later the great trio records), and Henry Grimes, whose bowed solo on Raoul is one of the few of its era on record (S2). Discovery value is high and the canon holds no Haynes leader album at all.

personnel_record.notes: Two sessions at Van Gelder Studio, Englewood Cliffs, NJ: May 16, 1962 (matrix 10926-10929 — 'If I Should Lose You', 'Raoul', 'Snap Crackle', 'Fly Me to the Moon') and May 23, 1962 (10932-10934 — 'Long Wharf', 'Moon Ray', 'Some Other Spring') (S3, obs; corroborated by S1 infobox 'May 16 & 23, 1962' at Van Gelder Studio, and S2 'Recording Date May 16, 1962 & May 23, 1962'). Producer Bob Thiele and engineer Rudy Van Gelder per the JazzProfiles discography transcription of the album credits (S4, obs; Thiele independently confirmed by S1 infobox). Liner notes by Stanley Dance (S4). One fixed quartet across both dates — the sessionography lists a single roster with no substitutions (S3). Title spelling conflict: AllMusic prints the opening track as 'Moonray' (S2) while Wikipedia and the Impulse! catalog use 'Moon Ray' (S1, S3); the original printed form 'Moon Ray' is retained and the variant recorded here. A January 15, 1963 edit session in New York produced 45-rpm edits (11293-11294) of 'Snap Crackle' and 'Fly Me to the Moon' (S3) — not part of this album and excluded. Reissue CD Impulse! IMPD-180 (1996) adds no bonus tracks; the seven-track program is the original LP. AllMusic styles: Bop, Hard Bop (S2); Wikipedia genres: post-bop, modal jazz (S1); style_primary recorded as post-bop.

ballot.album: Roy Haynes — Out of the Afternoon (1962)
ballot.case_for: JazzProfiles reports that Haynes named this his favorite leader date (S4), making it a particularly persuasive opportunity to hear a foundational modern-jazz drummer directing his own ensemble. Kirk, Flanagan, and Grimes give the quartet exceptional session gravity (S3), while AllMusic’s praise for Haynes’s lightly dancing accompaniment supports its value as an immediately engaging introduction to conversational post-bop drumming (S2). Favorable assessments from AllMusic, contemporary Down Beat, Penguin, and Rolling Stone, as collected in S1, reinforce an artistic case built on distinctive ensemble chemistry rather than historical obligation.
ballot.case_against: The evidence establishes a highly admired session more securely than a load-bearing canonical landmark: favorable ratings are not equivalent to repeated core-collection selections, and most are available here only through S1’s secondary compilation. Haynes’s personal preference supports the defining-statement argument but does not establish the album’s wider historical authority, while the dossier supplies no direct testimony demonstrating downstream influence. Its personnel connections and modal affinities establish lineage and context, but treating those connections as proof that this particular record changed subsequent practice would overstate the evidence.
ballot.disagreement: Reference 2 judges the leader statement and ensemble achievement sufficient for consensus_core; Reference 1 assigns contested because independent canonical recognition and album-specific influence remain insufficiently demonstrated. Both agree on strong priority and unambiguous scope. Reference 1’s attempted factual correction is itself mistaken: Tommy Flanagan did play on Giant Steps, so that objection carries no weight.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes that John give this strong, contested candidate a focused listen as a potential Haynes leader statement, without treating its core-canon status as settled.
